claim: Larger language models are well-calibrated on diverse multiple-choice and true/false questions when the questions are provided in the right format.
stance_target: LLM scale improves calibration on structured question-answering, motivating optimism about self-evaluation
scope_conditions: Multiple-choice and true/false QA tasks, larger models specifically (scale-dependent finding)
quoted_support: We first show that larger models are well-calibrated on diverse multiple choice and true/false questions when they are provided in the right format.

claim: Models can self-evaluate open-ended answers by proposing an answer and then estimating the probability P(True) that the proposed answer is correct, with performance improving further when the model considers multiple of its own sampled answers before judging validity of one.
stance_target: Reflective/verbalized self-evaluation is a viable calibration mechanism for open-ended generation
scope_conditions: Open-ended sampling tasks, diverse array of task types
quoted_support: we can approach self-evaluation on open-ended sampling tasks by asking models to first propose answers, and then to evaluate the probability "P(True)" that their answers are correct. We find encouraging performance, calibration, and scaling for P(True)... Performance at self-evaluation further improves when we allow models to consider many of their own samples before predicting the validity of one specific possibility.

claim: A trained P(IK) ('probability I know') estimate, computed without reference to any specific proposed answer, performs well and partially generalizes across tasks but struggles with calibration when applied to genuinely new/unseen tasks.
stance_target: Trained confidence estimators transfer robustly across task domains without recalibration
scope_conditions: Cross-task generalization of a trained P(IK) probe
quoted_support: Models perform well at predicting P(IK) and partially generalize across tasks, though they struggle with calibration of P(IK) on new tasks.
